title: Microsoft Purview: apply default SharePoint library labels to existing files (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: the licensing guidance is no longer accurate. Microsoft now explicitly requires a qualifying premium subscription for library default labeling, and client-only P2 entitlement must not be presented as sufficient for service-side labeling. The encryption restriction also needs its documented qualification.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to apply a SharePoint library's default sensitivity label to existing files.
claims.quote: Enables auto-labeling of existing SharePoint files to match the default sensitivity label configured on their document library.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes closing labeling gaps for data at rest without relying on manual user labeling.
claims.quote: This helps organizations close labeling gaps for data at rest and ensure consistent, secure-by-default protection across SharePoint libraries—without relying on manual user labeling.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators to review simulation results before turning on the existing-files policy.
claims.quote: Review the simulation results before you turn on the policy to confirm that the expected SharePoint sites, document libraries, default library labels, and files are included.

claims.claim: A label configured with markings or other settings could appear on many existing files when the policy runs.
claims.quote: If the labels you select are configured to use visual markings (headers, footers, watermarks), these markings aren't applied to documents when you use auto-labeling.
claims.fix: Replace 'Once such a policy runs, a label with encryption, markings or other settings could appear on many existing files.' with 'Once such a policy runs, many eligible existing files could receive the library default label and its encryption. Visual markings are not applied to documents by auto-labeling.'

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: A label that applies encryption can change who can open a file.
claims.quote: Can be decrypted only by users authorized by the label's encryption settings.

claims.claim: Labels with user-defined permissions do not support a default label for a library.
claims.quote: Let users assign permissions when they apply the label and the checkbox In Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, prompt users to specify permissions is selected.
claims.fix: Replace 'labels with user-defined permissions' with 'labels configured with Let users assign permissions when they apply the label and with In Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, prompt users to specify permissions selected'. Keep the separate expiry and Double Key Encryption restrictions.

claims.claim: Labels with User access to content expires set to anything other than Never do not support library defaults.
claims.quote: User access to content expires is set to a value other than Never.

claims.claim: Labels configured with Double Key Encryption do not support library defaults.
claims.quote: Double Key Encryption is selected.
